stories.title: Andy Burnham arrives in Ukraine with plans to share UK blueprints for long-range missiles – Europe live
stories.summary: The Kremlin responded to Burnham’s overnight comments, saying his plans to help Ukraine make its own long-range cruise missiles would “add fuel to the fire” in bilateral British-Russian relations. Asked about UK prime minister Andy Burnham’s visit to Kyiv on Monday and the new British missile support, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Britain was a participant in the war on Ukraine’s side and accused London of doing everything it could to prevent any progress towards an eventual peace deal. (Goes without saying that this isn’t really true.) As mentioned earlier, Ukraine is celebrating its independence day today, andthe Coalition of the Willing will be meeting soon for the latest round of talks on helping Ukraine, on the 35th anniversary of Ukraine’s Independence Day (10:39). And I will bring you all the key events here, obviously. “Britain is methodically and regularly throwing oil on the fire and methodically and regularly plotting schemes to prevent even the slightest progress in the peace process.” He added that Russia would target and “destroy” facilities producing the missile in Ukraine. The UK prime minister will use the trip to announce that the UK government will allow the European defence company MBDA to declassify information about UK-made components of the Anglo-French Storm Shadow/Scalp missiles to help Ukraine build its own version. While the announcement will probably take years to have an impact on the war,it is likely to escalate tensions with Moscow at an already fraught moment in UK-Russian relations. “On Ukraine’s 35th anniversary of independence, the Ukrainian people should be in no doubt: the UK is behind you today and for as long as it takes. I am proud of the contribution our country has made to Ukraine and I want the Ukrainian people to hear it directly from me that our support will not waver. After all, Ukraine’s security is our security.

stories.title: 'Half my business will be gone' - Firms in Canada and US fear trade war
stories.summary: Cindy Baldassi relies on American buyers to keep her stone-and-glass jewellery company going. Some 75% of sales of pieces including amethyst, sea glass and agates from her business, CindyLouWho2, based in Calgary, Alberta, come from Americans. But after trade talks between the US and Canada collapsed over the weekend and leaders of both countries pledged to slap 50% tariffs on each other's products, business owners on both sides of the border are bracing for the fallout. With a majority of the items she sells falling under US President Donald Trump's newly imposed tariffs, Baldassi says she will need to add 50% to the price of most of her products to stay afloat. "It's quite likely that it will wipe out most of my US sales," Baldassi told the BBC. "I expect that at least half of my business will be gone." Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has pledged levies starting on 8 September on US steel, dairy, appliances and electronics. Trump tariffs went into effect on Saturday, hitting Canadian wine, dairy, cement, clothing and hockey equipment. In Canada, it is not clear how much more severe the impacts will be, since the country has grown somewhat used to the on-again-off-again trade war. Lind Furniture has been in business for almost 60 years in the Canadian province of Ontario, selling leather furniture to big store clients like Sears and Costco over the years. Sales dropped when Trump took office in 2025. "As soon as there were tariffs in the air, people put purchases on hold," Michael Saifer, general manager of Lind Furniture, told the BBC.

stories.title: Russia increases steel production by 3.3% to 5.7 mln metric tons in July — WSA
stories.summary: Global steel production amounted to 149.2 mln metric tons in July 2026, down 0.3% from a year earlier
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 24.
Steel production in Russia increased by 3.3% in July 2026 compared with the same period in 2025, reaching 5.7 mln metric tons, according to a report by the World Steel Association (WSA).
According to the association’s report, China produced 76.9 mln metric tons of steel in July, down 3.6% from July 2025, while India produced 14.4 mln metric tons, up 1.9%.
Steel production in Japan increased by 0.4% in July to 6.9 mln metric tons, while production in the United States rose by 4.4% to 7.4 mln metric tons.
Steel production by Russia and other CIS countries, as well as Ukraine, amounted to 6.7 mln metric tons in July 2026, up 2.2% from a year earlier.
Countries in Asia and Oceania produced 109.4 mln metric tons of steel in July, down 1.2%.
EU countries produced 10.5 mln metric tons of steel, up 3.8% from a year earlier.
Steel production in North America increased by 4.9% in July to 9.6 mln metric tons.
South American countries produced 3.6 mln metric tons of steel during the reporting period, up 2.8%.
Middle Eastern countries produced 3.8 mln metric tons of steel, down 13.4% from the same period a year earlier.
Overall, global steel production amounted to 149.2 mln metric tons in July 2026, down 0.3% from a year earlier, according to the association’s report.
The World Steel Association is one of the world’s largest industry associations.

stories.title: Armenia, having applied for EU membership, to face contradictions in EAEU — Kremlin
stories.summary: According to Dmitry Peskov, Armenia will need to initiate a comprehensive process of aligning its legislation with European standards across various sectors
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 24.

Following Armenia’s application for European Union membership, Yerevan is poised to face significant contradictions within the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), a development that could ultimately prove detrimental to Armenia’s interests, Russian Presidential Spokesman Dmitry Peskov has stated.

As he emphasized, "an important aspect that our representatives, including our head of state, have highlighted, is that after submitting an application for EU membership, Armenia will need to initiate a comprehensive process of aligning its legislation across various sectors – trade, phytosanitary measures, customs, and more – with European standards.
These standards are fundamentally inconsistent with those currently adopted throughout the EAEU.
This discord will lead to profound contradictions, which are likely to harm Armenia most of all."

The Kremlin spokesman clarified that this is precisely why the latest EAEU summit adopted a statement in which the heads of state of the union called on Armenia to hold a corresponding referendum as soon as possible.
